title: Typography Lab: family, size, weight, line-height, spacing
learningObjectives: Explain typography lab: family, size, weight, line-height, spacing and design an accessible interactive learning lab.

understand.concept: A Typography Lab lets learners adjust font family, size, weight, line-height, letter spacing, and text alignment while previewing a realistic sample. It should show the generated CSS and keep controls connected to one state model.
understand.whyItMatters: The lab should use labelled controls, a readable preview, sensible bounds, and fallback font stacks. Test long text and scripts with different glyph coverage; avoid controls that produce unreadable extremes.
understand.analogy: A typography lab is a typesetting desk where each control changes one aspect of the same sample text.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports understanding; a production lab needs real state management, safe preview isolation, and accessible controls.

explain.narrative: The starter synchronizes font size and line-height controls with a preview and CSS readout. Add the remaining typography controls as the task.

practise.guidedTask: Add controls for font family, weight, letter spacing, and alignment. Show generated CSS and test the preview with longer text and multiple scripts.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with labelled controls, a live preview, validation, reset behaviour, and a generated CSS readout. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Keep preview state and code output synchronized.
Handle invalid input without crashing the lab.
Keep learner content isolated from the parent application.
